chunks: 10. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Auramah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Abu al-Hasan al-Sha'iri, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:

Ibn al-Kawwa' came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful! By Allah, verily there is a verse in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, that has destroyed my heart and made me doubt my religion.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'May your mother be bereaved of you and deprived of you! What is that verse?'
The Word of Allah, the Exalted: 'And the birds with expanded wings, each knows its own prayer and its own glorification.'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O son of al-Kawwa'! Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has created angels in various shapes. But for Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, there is an angel in the form of a rooster, hoarse and gray. Its talons are in the seventh lower earth, and its dual comb is below the Throne. It has two wings; one in the East and one in the West. One is of fire and the other is of ice. When the time of prayer arrives, it stands on its talons, then raises its neck from below the Throne, and then flaps its two wings just as the roosters in your houses flap theirs. Neither the one from fire melts the ice, nor does the one from ice extinguish the fire. Then it calls out: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, He Alone, with no partner; and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Master of the Prophets and that his successor is the Master of the Successors, and that Allah is Pure, Holy, Lord of the Angels and the Spirit.'

He said: Then the roosters in your homes flap their wings and answer him with his call, and that is the Word of the Exalted: 'And the birds with expanded wings, each knows its own prayer and its own glorification,' referring to the roosters on earth.

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.ابن الكواء: Ibn al-Kawwa' (a companion of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological explanation for the verse about birds knowing their own prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam Ali (AS) elucidates the verse regarding birds' prayer by identifying a specific angel in the form of a rooster who proclaims the testimony of faith and the prophethood of Muhammad. This celestial rooster's call is mirrored by the physical roosters on earth, whose flapping wings and crowing serve as their form of prayer and glorification. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of linking cosmic phenomena to divine worship, reinforcing the concept that all creation, including animals, engages in *tasbih* (glorification) of Allah.
